heading: Iteration
text:
#### Iteration [IRET.28.6.6]

Iteration is **over the dense arrays by index**, not over probe slots: a
live count, and key and value accessors taking a position in `[0, len)`.

Because the payload is packed with no holes ([IRET.28.3]), a full walk
visits exactly `len` entries and skips nothing — an iteration costs the
number of live entries, not the capacity. This is why working-memory
walks do not degrade after a table has been heavily deleted from.

**Iteration order carries no meaning and must not be relied on.** It is
deterministic ([IRET.28.10.1]), but it reflects insertion and deletion
history — a delete moves the last entry into the freed position — so it is
neither insertion order nor stable across mutation. Anything requiring a
defined order sorts explicitly.

**Mutating during iteration invalidates it**, for the same reason: an
insert may grow and a delete relocates an entry, so indices shift beneath
the walk.
